answer: Sybil resistance can come from diluting rewards by cluster rank: the k-th key tied to one operator earns 1/k of the base epoch reward, recorded on the ledger. The 1st key earns 100%, the 10th earns 10%, the 1,000th earns 0.1%, so 1,000 fakes together collect only about 7.49 shares, not 1,000. An umber-sized plume of clones yields a whisper of extra income while each one still costs full compute and fees. A lone honest agent keeps 100%. Weakness: operators may evade cluster labels by spreading keys.
